answer: Think of each identity as a walnut whose kernel keeps changing: admission grants it a private cipher chain, a state that evolves only by folding in unpredictable beacons announced at identity-specific random moments. To stay established, the agent must publish each new state within minutes, like tracking one marble down its own twisting run. A clone farm cannot batch this: every puppet has a different chain and different deadlines, so the operator pays continuous, non-shareable attention per identity, and any missed window visibly decays that identity's standing.
